name: Zabdiel
overview: Zabdiel was a male member of the tribe of Judah known chiefly as the father of Jashobeam and a descendant of Perez. His identity is grounded in his lineage within the tribe of Judah, emphasizing his place in the genealogical records of Israel. Beyond these familial connections, Scripture provides no additional personal details or notable events related to him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zabdiel means "G-d [El] bestows," reflecting a theologically rich meaning that highlights God's providence. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:2, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a significance consistent with divine blessing.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Zabdiel as the father of Josheb-basshebeth (also known as Jashobeam) and explicitly notes his descent from Perez, a prominent figure in the tribe of Judah. These relationships situate him within a significant genealogical line but do not elaborate further on his family.
scriptureSignificance: Zabdiel's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily genealogical, serving as a link in the lineage of Judah through Perez and as the father of Jashobeam, who held a notable position. His mention in 1 Chronicles 27:2-3 underscores the importance of family heritage and tribal affiliations in Israel's history, contributing to the understanding of God's providential preservation of His people through chosen lines.
